faq_slots.question: Are you insured?
faq_slots.answer_brief: The cover figure from [CV: insurance_cover] and what the cover is for (the dog, the owner and other people during a session). Never which policy a trainer must hold: the trade facts Table G says no universal requirement is verified.

faq_slots.question: What happens if something goes wrong?
faq_slots.answer_brief: From [CV: complaints_process] only.

faq_slots.question: Do you guarantee your training?
faq_slots.answer_brief: Used only when a guarantee is confirmed in the client values. Start with yes, then the terms exactly as given, as what the business does about a session the owner is not happy with. Never a behaviour outcome, a timeline or the word cured.

faq_slots.question: What if the training isn't working for my dog?
faq_slots.answer_brief: Used when nothing in cover_chain other than insurance is confirmed. Open with what the owner does: tell us, and the plan is looked at again. Then that progress happens between sessions and depends on the practice at home, and that a behaviour which changed suddenly, or an older dog that is not shifting, means a vet check first (the trade facts Table A: behaviour modification). Then the reasonable care and skill standard every service works to, as the standard the work is held to, never as a defence. No promise of an outcome, no promise to come back or put it right for free. Never invent a guarantee.

faq_slots.question: How soon can you start?
faq_slots.answer_brief: From [CV: start_time] only, as given. Nothing about how long the training takes (the trade facts Table A: duration varies, no standard).

faq_slots.question: Is the quote free and no obligation?
faq_slots.answer_brief: From [QUOTE_FREE] and [CV: quote_method].

faq_slots.question: How do your quotes work?
faq_slots.answer_brief: From [CV: quote_method] only.

faq_slots.question: How many sessions will my dog need?
faq_slots.answer_brief: No number: the trade facts Table A gives no standard duration for any training service and Table E says no set number of sessions establishes reliable recall. Give what decides it (the behaviour, how long it has been practised, the dog's age, how often the owner practises between sessions) and that the plan is reviewed as you go. Never a timeline or an outcome.

faq_slots.question: Why does my dog listen at home but not on walks?
faq_slots.answer_brief: Use the assigned symptom's meaning and its linked local issue (the walking environment: busy pavements, other dogs passing close by, livestock on the footpaths). Three genuinely different causes in plain words: the behaviour was learned in a quiet room and never rebuilt outside; the outdoors pulls the dog's focus off its owner (traffic, scents, another dog passing); every pull or outburst that works is rehearsed and gets stronger. Then what the local walks add, then how training builds it up in stages. Never blame the owner.

faq_slots.question: Will my dog only work for treats?
faq_slots.answer_brief: Food is the easiest reward to time well; play, a sniff and getting to move on count too. Say what a reward does in plain words (the trade facts Table E: a behaviour followed by something the dog values happens more often) and that rewards are used less often as the behaviour holds. Never a tool or method the words to avoid list names.

faq_slots.question: When should puppy training start?
faq_slots.answer_brief: From the trade facts Table E rows only: the early socialisation window, safe experiences at home before the vaccination course is finished, and classes that usually accept healthy puppies after their first vaccination, subject to the vet's advice. No age in weeks and no promise. Never that the owner should wait for every vaccination before any new experience.

why_titles_alt: Local Experience With Dogs Like Yours

cards.title: Angel indoors, a different dog outside
cards.brief: Sits and waits beautifully in the kitchen, then drags on the lead, shouts at every dog or ignores every call past the gate. The one cause this card makes: the cue was taught in a quiet room, and once outside the dog's focus is pulled off its owner by every scent, passing car and dog it meets. Say what the fix usually involves, in plain words: building it back up a step at a time, the garden first, then a quiet street, then somewhere busier (the trade facts Table A rows: practise in a quiet setting, add distractions, transfer to ordinary walks). Where the business runs its sessions only from the confirmed practices. The behaviour led services on the card list (recall, loose lead walking, obedience) follow this card. Never defiance, never that the owner has failed.
cards.mechanism: a cue taught indoors that was never taken outside

cards.title: It's getting worse, not better
cards.brief: Barking and lunging at dogs that started as a stare, chasing that started as interest, pulling that has grown since the dog was small. The one cause this card makes: every reaction that happens is practice, so the behaviour deepens rather than fades. Say what the fix usually involves: starting far enough away that the dog clocks the other dog and will still eat, then shortening that distance slowly (Table A: reactive dog training). Aggression that appears out of nowhere, or an older dog that starts behaving differently, means the vet before the trainer (Table A: behaviour modification). The reactivity, behaviour and aggression pages on the card list follow this card. Never a step by step plan for aggression, never 'cured', never a timeline. If the services list carries protection or security dog work (never otherwise): one sentence that a protection trained dog is first a dog under everyday control, and nothing more about that work on this page.
cards.mechanism: every reaction rehearsed, so it grows

cards.title: The puppy months and the teenage wobble
cards.brief: Mouthing, jumping up, crying when left, a puppy that hides from visitors; then, in adolescence, a recall that seems to vanish. The one cause this card makes: the first months and adolescence are when habits set, good or bad, so what is practised now tends to carry into adult life. Say what training usually involves at this stage: short practice, managed meetings with people, places and dogs, and keeping up the practice through the wobble (Table A: puppy training). When classes usually start, and what can begin at home before the vaccination course is finished, only from the trade facts Table E rows, with the vet's advice first; no age or week count the rows do not give. Puppy training follows this card as a care or routine led service. Never that the training has failed when adolescence hits.
cards.mechanism: habits setting while the dog grows up

cards.title: Home alone, and not coping
cards.brief: Crying or barking when the door shuts, chewing, a note from a neighbour, a dog pacing by the door at the first sound of keys. The one cause this card makes: the dog was never taught, in small steps, that being alone is safe. Say what usually helps: building up time alone gradually, worked on at home because that is where it happens (Table A: the row for nervous dogs). A vet's view first where the distress is severe or new (Table A). Where the services list includes day care or boarding: a day broken up with exercise, company and quiet time (Table A: dog day care). Never promise the dog will settle, never name a diagnosis, never that the owner leaves the dog too long.
cards.mechanism: being alone never taught in small steps

items.title: Practice in small steps, where the dog can succeed

items.title: Coaching you, not just the dog
items.brief: The owner's stage from the stages row: coach the owner, demonstrate the exercises, owner practice and review. Progress happens between sessions: say so once.

items.title: Taking it out into real walks

included.note: Fallback only: the tick items are the service's own Table A stages when the pack gives 6 or more; this set is used when it gives fewer (F-ITEMS-GENERIC). An item whose stage the row lacks is dropped, not invented.

cards.title: What you've noticed
cards.brief: The things an owner notices first, from the trade facts signs row for this service, in their words (pulls me, runs off, hides from visitors, growls when touched, won't settle). The one cause this card makes: the training left undone. Then what it leads to if left, from the skipped row: specific, never alarming, never a legal threat spelled out. For a boarding or day care page the signs are instead what a particular dog needs while it is away from home: how much it runs, how much it sleeps, whether it likes a crowd (Table A and Table B rows). For a skill led page (assistance, scent, gundog work) the card is what the dog is trained to do and which owner wants that, not a problem.

cards.title: Why what you tried didn't hold
cards.brief: The owner has usually tried something already: treats, a different lead or harness, a class, calling louder. The one cause this card makes: the reward or the practice came at the wrong moment or in the wrong place, never a lack of effort. Food that arrives a beat after the moment pays for the wrong thing; a new lead or harness changes how the walk feels, not the habit underneath; practice only in easy places leaves the hard walks unchanged (Table B done badly row). Say how this service rebuilds it, from the stages. Takes the shame away; never blames the owner, never names an aversive tool. Only on a protection or security dog page, where the services list includes it: the card is instead whether a dog is the right answer to the risk at all, with the honest cases where a dog is the wrong tool (a site the public walks through, a risk a camera already covers, a home that will not do the daily handling); no crime claim of any kind.
cards.mechanism: the timing of the reward, not the owner's effort

cards.title: When to see the vet first
cards.brief: A behaviour that changed suddenly, a growl when touched, an older dog that has stopped coping with things it used to. The one cause this card makes: pain or illness behind a change in behaviour, which training cannot reach. Say that a vet check comes first where the trade facts stages row has it (behaviour modification, reactive, nervous and anxious, aggressive dog work), as what the business does, never as a rule for the owner (Table E: no blanket requirement). For a boarding, day care or residential page the card is the health side of a stay instead: the records, the vaccination lead in and the screening before admission, from the trade facts rule rows only, with no figure. Never a diagnosis, never medical advice.
cards.mechanism: pain or illness behind a change in behaviour

cards.title: The right format for this dog
cards.brief: At home, on the usual walk, in a small class, a stay away. The one cause this card makes: a behaviour changes most reliably in the setting it happens in, so the format has to match the dog and the owner. Say which setting suits which dog from the stages row (home based work where the problem is at home; a class for a confident dog that needs practice around others; a stay only where the dog suits being away, Table A: residential dog training, assess suitability). A residential stay never replaces the owner's part: the handover and the practice at home (Table B and Table E: residential). Name only formats on the services list, with one sibling service page linked. Never that a stay fixes the dog.
cards.mechanism: the setting the behaviour happens in

cards.title: Walks that start on a busy pavement
cards.brief: Narrow pavements, shared stairwells, a front door that opens straight onto the street, dogs passing within a lead's length of each other. The one cause this card makes: dogs meeting nose to nose with nowhere to pass, so lead manners and a reactive dog's calm are tested on every walk; the town profile and the allocated neighbourhoods say which streets (terraces, flats, the centre). Say what it means for training in plain words (lead work and distance come before anything else here); what the business does only from confirmed practices. Not a behaviour learned indoors, not a reaction rehearsed: the town's category and service pages own those.
cards.mechanism: dogs meeting nose to nose with nowhere to pass

cards.title: Footpaths through fields with stock in them
cards.brief: Paths that cross grazing, a stile into a field of sheep, lambing fields at the edge of town. The one cause this card makes: livestock within reach of a dog off the lead, which is a legal matter for the owner and a danger to the dog. The normal case, with 'usually' and from the trade facts rule rows only (a lead near stock, a lead on open land in the season the row gives; never the Act's name, a date or a distance). Say why a reliable recall and a stop cue are built before the dog is let off here. Never an invented incident.
cards.mechanism: livestock within reach of a dog off the lead

cards.title: Dogs that spend the working day alone
cards.brief: Commuter streets, new estates of young families, a dog that barks through the afternoon. The one cause this card makes: a household out all day and a dog with nothing to do, from the town profile where it gives who lives here. Say what it means for training (settling, short practice that fits a working week) and, where the services list includes day care or boarding, what a day with exercise, company and rest changes (Table A: dog day care). Never that the town's owners neglect their dogs. Not being alone never taught in small steps: the category page owns that.
cards.mechanism: a household out all day and a dog with nothing to do

cards.title: Places where the lead rules change
cards.brief: A beach closed to dogs in summer, a park with a dogs on leads order, a nature reserve with ground nesting birds. The one cause this card makes: parks and beaches with their own dog orders, which change what a walk there asks of the dog; from the dossier rules only, as what usually applies, never the order's name. Say what that asks of the training (a reliable recall and a settled walk on the lead both matter here). Where the dossier gives no such rule, the card is the town's one open space and what practising there involves.

faq_slots.question: What if the training isn't working for my dog?
faq_slots.answer_brief: Open with what the owner does: tell us, and the plan is looked at again. Then that progress happens between sessions and depends on the practice at home, and that a behaviour which changed suddenly, or an older dog that is not shifting, means a vet check first (Table A: behaviour modification). Then the reasonable care and skill standard every service works to, as the standard, never as a defence. No promise of an outcome, no promise to come back free. Never invent a guarantee.

faq_slots.question: What happens when I get in touch from [TOWN]?
faq_slots.answer_brief: From [CV: quote_method] and the confirmed practices only: what the owner sends (the dog's age, what it does and where, what they have tried), what the business looks at, what comes back. No timescale unless [CV: response_time] is set. Never a number of sessions.

faq_slots.question: When is the right time to start training?
faq_slots.answer_brief: The life stages in plain words: puppyhood (classes usually accept healthy puppies after their first vaccination, with the vet's advice, from the trade facts Table E only; no age in weeks), adolescence, when a dog appears to forget what it knew and that is normal, adult dogs, where change comes from building a stronger habit in place of the old one, and older dogs, where a change in behaviour means a vet check first. The reason not to wait: every reaction practised gets stronger. No dates, no timeline, no outcome.
